title: Build a catalog of data collaborations
summary: Develop a trusted catalog where people can discover concrete data projects and organizations can eventually propose work for review.
workAvailable: Classify opportunities by domain, skills, participation model, and readiness
Identify missing, overlapping, and potentially redundant initiatives
Design a reviewed submission path for teams, labs, and organizations
caveats: Direct submissions are not available yet.
Every published opportunity still requires editorial verification and clear attribution.

title: Map payroll concepts across organizations
attribution: This student project began at IES N.º 7 before Conjecture 56 was created. That experience helped shape Conjecture 56's approach to educational and institutional collaboration.
summary: Create a reproducible, human-reviewed crosswalk between payroll concepts used by different public organizations.
workAvailable: Define the canonical data contract and semantic relationship vocabulary
Normalize source spreadsheets through organization-specific adapters
Build and evaluate an explainable candidate-ranking baseline
caveats: The current repository and proposal are not public contribution entry points.
Students propose and evaluate mappings; domain specialists retain final authority.
Payroll records require strict privacy controls and authorized data access.

title: Govern shared AI API access
summary: Provide teams with individually governed model access while keeping upstream credentials protected.
workAvailable: Deployed Bifrost virtual keys with per-key and per-model quotas
Added self-service usage and limit inspection
Kept provider credentials server-side and documented secure client onboarding
caveats: Access is provisioned deliberately rather than through public self-registration.
Provider limits remain authoritative when they are stricter than local quotas.

title: Measure the Spanish–English LLM gap under prompting
summary: Measure the performance gap between Spanish and English in small open language models under zero-shot prompting, using the ODESIA Leaderboard (UNED) controlled bilingual benchmark. Planned as an applied research project to propose at UCSE.
workAvailable: Register on the ODESIA Leaderboard and download the bilingual task datasets it distributes
Design zero-shot and few-shot prompts, starting with the four public Extended Tasks
Run small open models (<8B) through the Conjecture 56 gateway and record predictions
Submit EvALL-format predictions and read the calibrated Spanish–English gap per task
Publish the prompting-mode gap analysis as an open applied research report
caveats: Proposed as an applied research project at Universidad Católica de Santiago del Estero (UCSE); no manual data creation is required because every dataset is an existing annotated benchmark.
Core Task test labels stay private at UNED; confirm how prompting-mode systems are categorized before extending beyond the Extended Tasks.
Fine-tuning variants can use free Kaggle or Colab GPU tiers; zero-shot inference runs on the Conjecture 56 gateway.

title: Student AI Access Pilot Program
summary: Give students managed access to language models when they actively contribute to a project listed by Conjecture 56.
workAvailable: Provisioned an individual virtual key for each participating student
Applied bounded model, daily, monthly, and request-rate limits
Enabled students to inspect their own usage without exposing other keys
caveats: The program currently serves participating students from Prácticas Profesionalizantes III at IES N.º 7 and Inteligencia Artificial at UCSE.
Course enrollment alone does not grant access; students must contribute to a project listed by Conjecture 56.
Keys are individual, scoped, monitored, and revocable.

title: OpenHands
summary: Open-source platform for AI software agents, with documented enterprise use in engineering and automation workflows.
calls: Registration required: Community Call on 2026-12-03; all are welcome, but no recurring cadence is confirmed.
caveats: The C3 AI case is vendor-produced; no independent deployment audit was found.
Confirm current priorities with maintainers before starting.

title: Argo Workflows
summary: Kubernetes-native workflow engine used in production by major organizations and by Kubeflow Pipelines and Metaflow.
calls: Open and recurring: monthly community meeting with public notes and recordings.
caveats: Large backlog; agree on scope with maintainers before coding.

title: Kubeflow
summary: Machine learning platform for Kubernetes, adopted by research and enterprise teams for pipelines, training, and model operations.
calls: Open and recurring: multiple public meetings with LFX/Zoom registration, notes, and recordings.
caveats: Exact cadence lives in the LFX calendar, not the static community page.

title: Tekton Pipelines
summary: Cloud-native CI/CD framework used at scale and as the foundation of OpenShift Pipelines and Konflux.
calls: Open and recurring: weekly community meeting alternating regional times.
caveats: Some documentation uses legacy timezone labels; confirm local time in the calendar.

title: Apache Beam
summary: Unified batch and streaming pipeline model used by large-scale data platforms and MLOps teams.
calls: No verified recurring call: public calendar and events exist, but no general recurring meeting is clearly documented.
caveats: Coordination is mainly through the mailing list; confirm priorities there.

title: Backstage
summary: Developer portal and platform-engineering framework used to catalog services, infrastructure, and automation.
calls: Open and recurring: monthly community session with a public agenda and recordings.
caveats: The static roadmap is out of date; use the pinned 2026 issue and active issues.

title: LM Evaluation Harness
summary: Standard open harness for reproducible language-model evaluation, including multilingual benchmarks and backend integrations.
calls: No verified recurring project call: coordination happens through GitHub and Discord.
caveats: Prompt and backend choices can change scores and rankings; reproducibility does not guarantee validity.

title: MLCommons Croissant
summary: Metadata standard that makes machine-learning datasets discoverable and loadable across major catalogs and frameworks.
calls: Registration required: weekly Wednesday working-group meeting; registration and Google authentication are required.
caveats: Access is authenticated; silent participation is not explicitly guaranteed for ordinary registrants.

title: Xarray
summary: Core library for labeled multidimensional arrays, widely used in climate, geoscience, and scientific data workflows.
calls: Open and recurring: biweekly developer meeting. Listeners are explicitly welcome.
caveats: The base roadmap is dated 2021; use current issues to choose work.

title: Zarr and Zarr-Python
summary: Open storage format and Python implementation for large, chunked scientific arrays in cloud and high-performance environments.
calls: Open and recurring: biweekly community and Zarr-Python meetings, open to all.
caveats: No explicit silent-listener policy; visible meeting notes lag the current calendar.

title: OpenLineage
summary: Open standard for collecting data lineage and operational metadata across pipelines and analytics tools.
workAvailable: Integrations with Airflow, Spark, dbt, and Flink
calls: Open and recurring: monthly meeting on the third Wednesday, with RSVP, notes, and recordings.
caveats: Impact is mainly enabling infrastructure rather than a final application.

title: OpenMetadata
summary: Open platform for data catalog, quality, lineage, and governance across organizational data assets.
calls: Open and recurring: biweekly meeting with public recordings.
caveats: Adoption figures and case studies are project- or vendor-reported.

title: OpenML
summary: Open platform for sharing datasets, tasks, and reproducible machine-learning experiments.
calls: No verified recurring call: the project organizes occasional hackathons.
caveats: Coordinate large changes in an issue before implementing them.

title: SciPy
summary: Foundational scientific Python library used across numerical computing, signal processing, optimization, and machine learning.
calls: No recurring call: community meetings were cancelled in August 2025.
caveats: Do not rely on older pages that still announce the cancelled meetings.

title: OpenTelemetry
summary: Vendor-neutral observability standard and tooling for traces, metrics, logs, and AI-agent instrumentation.
workAvailable: Semantic conventions for AI and agents
calls: Open and recurring: multiple SIG calls. The GenAI SIG meets weekly and accepts listeners.
caveats: The ecosystem is fragmented; choose one SIG before proposing work.

title: KServe
summary: Kubernetes-native model-serving platform used in production for predictive and generative AI workloads.
calls: Open and recurring: biweekly public working group.
caveats: Requires Kubernetes and usually Go or Python; there is no single roadmap as clear as Flux's.

title: vLLM
summary: High-throughput inference engine for large language models, used in production services and open-model deployments.
calls: Open and recurring: office hours every two weeks, open and recorded.
caveats: Full development usually requires GPUs and expensive CI; AI-assisted contributions must be disclosed under project policy.

title: OpenCost
summary: Open cost-monitoring platform for Kubernetes and AI infrastructure, with emerging inference-cost coverage.
calls: Open and recurring: every two weeks, alternating regions.
caveats: Adopter list is relatively short and self-reported; AI costing is still maturing.

title: Flux
summary: GitOps toolkit for continuous delivery and reproducible Kubernetes infrastructure.
calls: Open and recurring: weekly meeting and bug scrubs, public and recorded.
caveats: Large changes require RFCs and API compatibility review.

title: Kyverno
summary: Policy-as-code engine for Kubernetes security, compliance, and supply-chain controls.
calls: Open and recurring: weekly community meeting; joining the Google Group is required.
caveats: Joining the Google Group is required for meeting invitations.

title: Falco
summary: Runtime security project for detecting anomalous behavior in containers, Kubernetes, and Linux hosts.
calls: Open and recurring: biweekly meeting with a public calendar.
caveats: Engine work requires Linux, eBPF, and C++; rules and documentation are easier entry points. The visible roadmap was last updated in 2024.

title: ModelBench and AILuminate
summary: Open benchmarks and tooling for evaluating AI safety, jailbreaks, and reliability.
calls: Registration required: weekly AI Risk and Reliability meeting; registration and approval are required.
caveats: AILuminate does not certify that a system is safe; it measures specific risks.

title: MedPerf
summary: Open platform for federated evaluation of medical AI models without centralizing clinical data.
calls: No verified recurring call: the Medical group accepts registrations but has no upcoming recurring meeting published.
caveats: Clinical use is research-stage; no patient-outcome improvement is demonstrated.

title: OpenMRS
summary: Open electronic medical record platform deployed in low-resource health systems and national programs.
calls: Open and recurring: weekly Squads Call. Listeners are explicitly welcome.
caveats: National deployments require domain and health-informatics context.

title: OHDSI ATLAS
summary: Open application for observational health research over federated OMOP data.
calls: Open and recurring: weekly community call, open and recorded; ATLAS also has its own workgroup.
caveats: Observational evidence does not establish causality.

title: OpenTripPlanner
summary: Open multimodal journey-planning platform used by public transport agencies.
calls: Open and recurring: development meetings twice a week and a monthly product meeting; access is documented in governance.
caveats: Contributions require two approvals from different organizations; agree on scope first.

title: Open Food Facts Robotoff
summary: Open Food Facts service that extracts and validates food-product information for public health and consumer apps.
calls: Open and recurring: first Tuesday of each month via public Google Meet.
caveats: The page calls the meeting weekly, but the published rule is monthly.

title: HOT Tasking Manager
summary: Humanitarian mapping coordination platform used by relief organizations and open mapping communities.
calls: Confirmation required: monthly open meetings existed, but the available source is old; confirm the current calendar.
caveats: The available meeting source is from 2023; confirm it is still active.

title: PyPSA
summary: Open energy-system modelling framework used for capacity expansion and planning analysis.
calls: No verified fixed recurring call: user meetings and recordings exist, but no fixed public cadence is documented.
caveats: User meetings are not a fixed recurring public call.
